question: Forward right turn oscillation after sustained travel: fixed direction/delay/noise comparisons

noise_profiles.delay15-noise: fixed 3 physics-step actuator delay, training observation noise enabled
noise_profiles.delay30-noise: fixed 6 physics-step actuator delay, training observation noise enabled
noise_profiles.delay15-clean: fixed 3 physics-step actuator delay, policy observation corruption disabled

method.command: 10s stand, 30s forward 0.5m/s, 30s forward 0.5m/s plus yaw -0.6/right or +0.6/left, 20s zero command
method.estimated_velocity_error: pre-action student estimate minus same-step pre-action true velocity, m/s; no comparison against post-step root velocity
method.hip_target: raw action first two values (right,left)*0.25; physical hip velocity/torque selected by joint names
method.exclusions: Done sample and following 49 samples excluded from phase/chunk summaries; diff metrics require consecutive steps. Official full metrics kept separately.
method.utilization: abs(sampled applied torque or joint speed) / recorded simulator limits, not an independently measured hardware saturation
method.direction_check: Both directions must have identical samples before turn command; verified per variant below

limitations: No hardware recording and actual incident commands unknown. These scenarios are controlled hypotheses, not a reconstruction of the physical incident.
Fixed command-buffer delay covers only one part of end-to-end physical latency.
One seed, nominal plane/mechanics, no pushes, one speed and turn magnitude.
No measured contact or instantaneous per-physics-substep torque telemetry; absence of sampled saturation does not prove no substep saturation.
No approved convergence/safety thresholds; a completed case or zero resets does not establish hardware safety.
User reports a severe physical incident; continue pausing physical reproduction regardless of these bounded simulation outcomes.
